facts: Avoid generalising about an entire state or community.
Do not rank cultures as superior or inferior.
Look for connections as well as differences.
Use reliable sources rather than stereotypes.

cards.title: Unity check
cards.question: Does unity in diversity mean that everyone has identical customs?
cards.answer: No. It means people with different customs and identities can live together with mutual respect and shared civic values.

cards.title: Example check
cards.question: Give two examples of cultural diversity in India.
cards.answer: Examples include languages, regional foods, clothing, festivals, music, dance and art forms.

chapters.title: Family and Community
chapters.subtitle: Exploring Society: India and Beyond · quick recall

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: Families and communities are groups in which people care for one another, share responsibilities and cooperate. Their forms and roles can differ across places and time.

cards.title: Remember and apply
cards.content: Notice the many kinds of work that support a community, including care work that may be unpaid or overlooked. Respect different family structures.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: How does a community help people meet needs that one family may not meet alone?
cards.answer: People share knowledge, services, resources and support; cooperation helps the community solve common problems.

cards.title: Family and community
cards.content: A family is a group of people connected through relationships and care. A community is a wider group connected by place, interests, identity or shared responsibilities.

cards.title: Different forms of support
facts: Helping with daily tasks and responsibilities.
Passing on skills, language and experience.

cards.title: Families can differ
cards.content: Families may be nuclear, extended, single-parent, blended or organised in other ways. What matters is care, respect, safety and responsibility, not one single family pattern.

left.heading: Family
left.content: Usually a close network of care and responsibility among related or chosen members.

right.heading: Community
right.content: A wider group that may include many families and individuals who share a place, interest or goal.

cards.title: Interdependence
cards.content: People rely on others for food, education, transport, healthcare, safety and emotional support. Communities work better when people cooperate and include everyone.

cards.title: Shared responsibilities
facts: Share age-appropriate tasks and care for belongings.
Respect others, cooperate and care for shared spaces.
Keep public spaces clean and help protect common resources.

cards.title: Community check
cards.question: How can a community help people meet needs that one family may not meet alone?
cards.answer: People share knowledge, services, resources and support; cooperation helps solve common problems.

cards.title: Inclusion check
cards.question: Why should community activities include people with different needs and abilities?
cards.answer: Inclusion allows everyone to participate, contribute and access shared opportunities with dignity.

chapters.title: Grassroots Democracy — Part 1: Governance
chapters.subtitle: Exploring Society: India and Beyond · quick recall

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: Governance is the way decisions are made and public services are organised. Democracy allows people to participate, choose representatives and hold decision-makers accountable.

cards.title: Remember and apply
cards.content: Think about why decisions should be made close to the people affected by them. Participation, transparency and accountability strengthen local governance.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What does accountability mean in a democracy?
cards.answer: People in authority must explain their decisions and can be questioned or held responsible for their actions.

cards.title: What is governance?
cards.content: Governance is the way decisions are made, rules are applied and public services are organised. It involves institutions, processes and people.

cards.title: Principles of good governance
facts: People can take part in decisions.
Decision-makers explain and answer for their actions.
Information and processes are open and understandable.
Rules apply fairly and protect rights.

cards.title: Democracy and participation
cards.content: Democracy is more than voting. People participate by discussing issues, asking questions, sharing views, attending local meetings and holding representatives accountable.

left.heading: Direct participation
left.content: People discuss or decide matters themselves, such as in a Gram Sabha meeting.

right.heading: Representative participation
right.content: People elect representatives who make decisions and work on their behalf.

cards.title: Why local governance matters
cards.content: Local institutions are closer to residents and can respond to local needs such as roads, water, sanitation, schools and community facilities.

cards.title: Governance check
cards.question: What does accountability mean in a democracy?
cards.answer: People in authority must explain their decisions and can be questioned or held responsible for their actions.

cards.title: Participation check
cards.question: Name two ways people can participate in democracy besides voting.
cards.answer: They can attend public meetings, raise local issues, submit suggestions, ask questions and monitor services.

chapters.title: Grassroots Democracy — Part 2: Local Government in Rural Areas
chapters.subtitle: Exploring Society: India and Beyond · quick recall

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: Rural local government works through institutions such as the Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti and Zila Parishad. The Gram Sabha includes adult voters of a village or Gram Panchayat area.

cards.title: Remember and apply
cards.content: The Gram Sabha provides a forum for people to discuss local needs and question the Panchayat. Different levels coordinate village, block and district work.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: Who are the members of a Gram Sabha?
cards.answer: All adult voters registered in the village or Gram Panchayat area are members of the Gram Sabha.

cards.title: Three tiers of rural local government
facts: Panchayat Samiti or equivalent block-level body.

cards.title: Gram Sabha
cards.content: The Gram Sabha includes all adult voters registered in the village or Gram Panchayat area. It provides a forum to discuss local needs, plans and the work of the Panchayat.

cards.title: Typical Gram Panchayat responsibilities
facts: Local roads, drains, sanitation and street lighting.
Village water supply and maintenance of local sources.
Local works and village development plans.
Local records and coordination with public schemes, as assigned by law.

cards.title: How a local issue can be raised
steps: Identify the issue and the people affected.
Discuss it with neighbours or the relevant ward or village representative.
Raise it in the Gram Sabha or appropriate public forum.
Ask what action, responsibility and timeline are proposed.
Follow up and review the result.

left.heading: Gram Sabha
left.content: The assembly of all registered adult voters in the village or Gram Panchayat area.

right.heading: Gram Panchayat
right.content: The elected local governing body that carries out assigned functions and works for the village area.

cards.title: Why decentralisation helps
cards.content: Decentralisation shares decision-making across levels of government. Local people can explain their needs directly and monitor local work.

cards.title: Gram Sabha check
cards.question: Who are the members of a Gram Sabha?
cards.answer: All adult voters registered in the village or Gram Panchayat area.

cards.title: Rural tier check
cards.question: Which institution works at the district level in the rural Panchayati Raj system?
cards.answer: The Zila Parishad.

chapters.title: Grassroots Democracy — Part 3: Local Government in Urban Areas
chapters.subtitle: Exploring Society: India and Beyond · quick recall

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: Urban local bodies manage services in towns and cities. Municipalities and Municipal Corporations work on issues such as water supply, roads, sanitation, street lighting and waste management.

cards.title: Remember and apply
cards.content: A city may be divided into wards represented by elected councillors. Citizens can raise local concerns through their ward representatives and civic bodies.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: Name two services commonly managed by an urban local body.
cards.answer: Examples include waste collection, sanitation, local roads, street lighting and water supply.

cards.title: Urban local bodies
facts: For a transitional area moving from rural to urban.
For a smaller urban area or town.
A local area represented by an elected councillor.

cards.title: Common urban civic services
facts: Providing and maintaining local water services.
Collection, transport and disposal or processing of waste.
Local streets, footpaths and street lighting.

cards.title: Ward councillors
cards.content: A city or town is divided into wards. Residents elect councillors to represent ward concerns and participate in the urban local body.

left.heading: Municipality
left.content: Usually governs a smaller urban area or town.

right.heading: Municipal Corporation
right.content: Usually governs a larger city with a broader administrative structure and service needs.

cards.title: Citizens and city services
cards.content: Urban services work best when residents use facilities responsibly, separate waste where required, avoid littering, conserve water and report faults through the correct channels.

cards.title: Urban service check
cards.question: Name two services commonly managed by an urban local body.
cards.answer: Examples include waste collection, sanitation, local roads, street lighting and water supply.

cards.title: Ward check
cards.question: Who represents residents of a ward in an urban local body?
cards.answer: An elected ward councillor.

chapters.title: The Value of Work
chapters.subtitle: Exploring Society: India and Beyond · quick recall

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: All kinds of work contribute to individuals, families and society. Work may be paid or unpaid, and care work is valuable even when it does not earn a wage.

cards.title: Remember and apply
cards.content: Recognise the skills and effort involved in different occupations. Respect workers and avoid judging the worth of work only by its income.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: Why is unpaid care work valuable to society?
cards.answer: It supports people's health, learning and daily life, making it possible for families and communities to function.

cards.title: Paid and unpaid work
cards.content: Paid work earns wages or income. Unpaid work may include caring for family members, cooking, cleaning, helping neighbours or volunteering. Both can create value.

cards.title: Types of work
facts: Looking after children, older people or someone who is unwell.
Cooking, cleaning, repairing and organising a home.
Volunteering, helping neighbours and maintaining shared spaces.
Producing or providing goods and services for payment.

cards.title: Why care work matters
cards.content: Care work supports health, learning, safety and everyday life. It often goes unnoticed because it is unpaid, but communities and economies depend on it.

left.heading: Paid work
left.content: Usually receives wages, salary or payment for a service or product.

right.heading: Unpaid work
right.content: May not earn money, but still takes time, effort and skill and benefits people or communities.

cards.title: Respect every occupation
cards.content: Work should not be judged by status or income alone. Different occupations require knowledge, effort and skill and contribute to society in different ways.

cards.title: Work value check
cards.question: Why is unpaid care work valuable to society?
cards.answer: It supports people's health, learning and daily life, helping families and communities function.

cards.title: Work classification
cards.question: A person volunteers to clean a neighbourhood park without payment. What kind of work is this?
cards.answer: Unpaid community work or volunteering.

chapters.title: Economic Activities Around Us
chapters.subtitle: Exploring Society: India and Beyond · quick recall

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: Economic activities involve producing, distributing and consuming goods and services. People work in many occupations to meet needs and earn livelihoods.

cards.title: Remember and apply
cards.content: Trace a product from its raw materials through production and transport to the person who uses it. Notice how producers, traders and consumers depend on one another.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What is the difference between a good and a service?
cards.answer: A good is a physical item that can be used, while a service is an activity or help provided to meet someone's need.

cards.title: Economic activities
facts: Moving goods and services to where people need them.
Using goods and services to meet needs and wants.

cards.title: Goods and services
cards.content: Goods are physical items that people can use, such as books, clothes or food. Services are activities or help provided to meet a need, such as teaching, transport or healthcare.

cards.title: Follow a product's journey
steps: Identify the raw materials needed.
Find out who produces or grows them.
Trace processing or manufacturing.
Follow transport, storage and sale.
Identify the consumer and how the product is used.

cards.title: People involved in an economy
facts: Makes or grows a good or provides a service.

cards.title: Interdependence in economic life
cards.content: A single product often depends on many people and activities. Farmers, factory workers, drivers, shopkeepers and consumers are connected through production and exchange.

left.heading: Needs
left.content: Things essential for life and basic well-being, such as food, water, shelter and healthcare.

right.heading: Wants
right.content: Things people would like to have; they vary with preferences, culture and circumstances.

cards.title: Goods or services?
cards.question: Is a haircut a good or a service?
cards.answer: A service, because it is an activity provided to a customer.

cards.title: Economic activity check
cards.question: What is the difference between a producer and a consumer?
cards.answer: A producer makes goods or provides services; a consumer uses them.

cards.title: Story / poem idea
cards.content: Rama Natha chases a magical potion instead of caring for his land. Sage Mahipati gives him a task that leads him to grow banana plants; Madhumati sells the fruit, and their steady work creates the wealth he wanted.

cards.title: Notice and explain
cards.content: The story contrasts a shortcut with patient effort. Notice how the sage guides Rama Natha through experience rather than simply arguing with him.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: Why does the sage ask Rama Natha to collect dew from banana leaves?
cards.answer: The task makes Rama Natha care for the plants over time. The real result is the banana harvest and the wealth earned through work, not a magic potion.

cards.title: Character and turning point
cards.content: Rama Natha is drawn to the promise of an easy magical solution. Sage Mahipati redirects him towards patient work; the growing banana plants and the sale of fruit reveal the practical source of prosperity.

cards.title: Important ideas to remember
facts: Wants to become wealthy through a magical shortcut.
Guides him through a task that teaches patience and effort.
Helps by selling the bananas grown from the plants.
A device in the story that motivates the work; not the real source of wealth.

cards.title: Theme and message
cards.content: The story values effort, patience, planning and practical action over magical shortcuts. Real success grows from useful work carried out consistently.

cards.title: Retell the story in sequence
steps: Rama Natha believes a potion can make him rich.
The sage gives him a task involving dew on banana leaves.
Rama Natha grows and cares for banana plants.
Madhumati sells the harvested bananas.
The family gains wealth through steady work, not magic.

cards.title: Explain the title
cards.question: Why is the bottle of dew an unlikely path to wealth?
cards.answer: The dew itself has no magical power; the task leads Rama Natha to grow and sell bananas, showing that work creates the real value.

cards.title: Story / poem idea
cards.content: A fox uses flattering words to make a raven show off its voice. When the raven opens its beak to sing, the food it holds falls and the fox gets it.

cards.title: Notice and explain
cards.content: Identify the fox's intention, the raven's weakness and the consequence. The fable warns readers to think carefully before trusting praise.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What lesson does the raven learn from the fox's flattery?
cards.answer: Do not let praise make you careless or proud; think about a speaker's motive before believing flattering words.

cards.title: Characters and their motives
cards.content: The fox wants the raven's food and uses praise as a trick. The raven enjoys the flattering words and forgets to hold on to its food while trying to sing.

cards.title: Fable structure
facts: The raven has food and sits in a tree.
The fox flatters the raven's voice.
The raven opens its beak; the food falls.
Beware of flattery and think about motives.

cards.title: Personification and dialogue
cards.content: Animals speak and behave like people in this fable. This makes the lesson easy to remember while allowing the reader to think about human behaviour.

left.heading: Flattery
left.content: Praise used to influence someone for the speaker's own benefit; it may be exaggerated or insincere.

right.heading: Genuine praise
right.content: Honest appreciation that does not manipulate the person being praised.

cards.title: Cause and effect
cards.question: What action causes the raven to lose its food?
cards.answer: The raven opens its beak to sing after hearing the fox's flattery, and the food falls.

cards.title: Story / poem idea
cards.content: This humorous folk tale uses a misunderstanding around the name Rama and a timely arrival to help expose a thief. Quick thinking turns a confusing situation into a rescue.

cards.title: Notice and explain
cards.content: Track who says or hears the name Rama and how the misunderstanding changes the events. Retell the sequence clearly rather than confusing the characters.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: How does the misunderstanding about the name Rama help in the story?
cards.answer: It creates confusion for the thief and helps the real person named Rama arrive at the right moment, leading to the thief being caught.

cards.title: How the rescue works
cards.content: The humour depends on the name Rama being misunderstood. Track who hears the name, what they think it means and how the confusion helps the real Rama arrive at the right moment.

cards.title: Story-reading checklist
facts: Identify the people involved in the misunderstanding.
Notice where the events take place.
Watch for the repeated name that causes confusion.
Notice when the real person arrives.
Explain how the thief is exposed or stopped.

cards.title: Humour through misunderstanding
cards.content: A word or name can be interpreted in more than one way. The story uses this confusion to create suspense and comedy.

cards.title: Write a clear plot summary
steps: Introduce the main characters and situation.
Explain the misunderstanding without skipping the clue.
Describe how each character reacts.
State how the misunderstanding is resolved.
End with the result of the rescue.

cards.title: Reading inference
cards.question: Why should a reader pay attention to how the name Rama is used in the dialogue?
cards.answer: The different interpretations of the name create the misunderstanding that drives the plot and helps the rescue happen.

cards.title: Story / poem idea
cards.content: Gajaraj, a royal elephant, feels lonely despite having every comfort. He and Buntee, a stray dog, become close friends; their separation makes both animals unhappy.

cards.title: Notice and explain
cards.content: Notice how friendship grows through kindness and shared time, not wealth or status. The story also shows that animals can form strong bonds.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: Why are Gajaraj and Buntee called unlikely best friends?
cards.answer: They are very different animals and come from different circumstances, yet they form a deep friendship through companionship and care.

cards.title: Character notes
facts: A royal elephant who has comfort but feels lonely.
A stray dog who becomes Gajaraj's close companion.
Grows through companionship, kindness and time spent together.
Their separation shows how much each depends on the friendship.

cards.title: Theme: friendship beyond difference
cards.content: The story shows that friendship is not limited by size, species, wealth or social position. Kindness and companionship create a meaningful bond.

left.heading: Material comfort
left.content: Food, shelter and possessions can meet physical needs.

right.heading: Emotional well-being
right.content: Companionship, trust and affection help meet emotional needs; comfort alone may not remove loneliness.

cards.title: Narrative point of view
cards.content: The narrator helps readers understand the feelings and behaviour of both animals. Their actions show affection even when they cannot explain it in human language.

cards.title: Inference
cards.question: Why does Gajaraj's friendship with Buntee matter even though Gajaraj already has a comfortable life?
cards.answer: The elephant is lonely; Buntee gives him companionship and affection that material comfort cannot provide.

cards.title: Story / poem idea
cards.content: The poem expresses a wish to be a thoughtful friend: to give one's best, accept others without unfair judgement and genuinely wish them well.

cards.title: Notice and explain
cards.content: Look for the speaker's promises and the values behind them. Explain how the poem describes friendship through actions and attitude.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What kind of friend does the speaker wish to be?
cards.answer: A caring, accepting and dependable friend who gives their best and does not judge others unfairly.

cards.title: Speaker and tone
cards.content: The speaker makes a personal promise about how to behave as a friend. The tone is sincere, warm and reflective rather than boastful.

cards.title: Values in the poem
facts: Respect a friend without unfair judgement.
Give one's best without keeping score.
Try to understand another person's feelings.

cards.title: Poetic voice
cards.content: The first-person voice makes the poem sound like a personal pledge. It invites readers to compare the speaker's promises with their own behaviour.

cards.title: Being a friend and having a friend

left.heading: Having a friend
left.content: Receiving companionship, help and understanding.

right.heading: Being a friend
right.content: Offering care, listening, honesty and support in return.

cards.title: Personal response
cards.question: Name two actions that show someone is a dependable friend.
cards.answer: Listening carefully, keeping promises, offering help, respecting differences and supporting a friend during difficulty.

cards.title: Story / poem idea
cards.content: Mario's grandfather uses an imaginary chair to help him discover which classmates are genuine friends. Their reactions reveal who supports him and who enjoys seeing him struggle.

cards.title: Notice and explain
cards.content: Distinguish real support from teasing or simply being present. The invisible-chair episode is a test of kindness and loyalty.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What does the invisible-chair test help Mario understand?
cards.answer: It helps him recognise classmates who genuinely care and support him instead of laughing when he faces difficulty.

cards.title: The invisible-chair test
facts: Wants to know which classmates are genuine friends.
Creates an imaginary-chair test to help Mario observe behaviour.
Classmates are invited to sit on an invisible chair; their reactions reveal their attitudes.
Real friendship is shown by kindness and support, not by teasing.

cards.title: How the test reveals character
cards.content: The imaginary chair is not a magic object; it is a situation that allows Mario to notice how classmates treat him when they think something unusual is happening.

cards.title: Theme: actions reveal friendship
cards.content: The story asks readers to judge friendship by behaviour—respect, kindness and support—rather than popularity or words alone.

cards.title: Analyse a character's behaviour
steps: Identify what the character says.
Notice what the character actually does.
Look at how the action affects another person.
Compare behaviour across the story.
Use evidence from events to support your judgement.

cards.title: Inference
cards.question: What does the invisible-chair test teach Mario about friendship?
cards.answer: It helps him recognise who genuinely cares and supports him instead of laughing at him or taking advantage of him.

cards.title: Story / poem idea
cards.content: Amber speaks with a personified neem tree and learns about its names, history and many uses in everyday life, traditional care and the environment.

cards.title: Notice and explain
cards.content: Personification gives the tree a voice. Separate the tree's real-life uses from the imaginative way the conversation is presented.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What literary device makes the neem tree speak to Amber?
cards.answer: Personification: the tree is given the human ability to speak and share its story.

cards.title: Neem tree: key uses
facts: Neem oil is obtained from seeds.
Trees provide habitat, help protect soil and contribute to local ecosystems.
Traditional uses are not a substitute for medical advice.

cards.title: Personification in Neem Baba
cards.content: The neem tree is given a human voice and speaks with Amber. Personification makes information about the tree engaging and encourages readers to listen to nature.

cards.title: Dialogue as a learning device
cards.content: Amber's questions guide the reader through the tree's identity, history and uses. Dialogue makes information feel like a conversation rather than a list.

cards.title: Vocabulary focus
facts: A tree known botanically as Azadirachta indica.
Connected with customs or practices passed through generations.
Related to the treatment or prevention of illness; claims should be evaluated carefully.
A figure of speech that gives human qualities to non-human things.

cards.title: Literary device
cards.question: Which literary device allows Neem Baba to speak to Amber?
cards.answer: Personification: the neem tree is given the human ability to speak.

cards.title: Story / poem idea
cards.content: The poem follows a young bird as its understanding of the world grows, moving from the shell to the nest, then to the wider world outside.

cards.title: Notice and explain
cards.content: Notice how each new stage changes the bird's view. The poem uses a growing perspective to show discovery and learning.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: How does the bird's idea of the world change as it grows?
cards.answer: Its world expands from the small space it first knows to the nest and then the wide world beyond.

cards.title: Stages in the bird's discovery
cards.content: The bird's understanding grows as its surroundings expand: first the shell, then the nest and finally the wider world. Each stage changes what the bird thinks the world contains.

cards.title: Images and ideas
facts: Represents the small world the young bird first knows.
A larger but still sheltered space.
Represents discovery, freedom and new experiences.

cards.title: Theme: learning through experience
cards.content: The poem suggests that what we know may be limited by what we have experienced. Curiosity and exploration help us revise our ideas.

cards.title: Poetic structure and perspective
cards.content: The repeated movement from one space to another creates a sense of gradual discovery. The reader follows the bird's changing point of view.

cards.title: Interpretation
cards.question: What does the bird's expanding world symbolise?
cards.answer: It symbolises growing knowledge and understanding as the bird gains new experiences.

cards.title: Story / poem idea
cards.content: A grandmother's letter introduces familiar kitchen spices and describes how they are used in traditional home care, food and everyday wellness.

cards.title: Notice and explain
cards.content: Recognise the spices and the uses described in the text, but distinguish traditional home practices from medical advice. Ask a trusted adult when unwell.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What is the main purpose of Daadi's letter about spices?
cards.answer: To share knowledge of common spices and their traditional uses, showing how food, culture and everyday care are connected.

cards.title: Ideas in the letter
facts: Common ingredients used in cooking and traditional home practices.
Passes knowledge and family experience to a younger generation.
Recipes and ingredients carry memories and traditions.
Traditional remedies should not replace professional medical care.

cards.title: Letter format
cards.content: A personal letter usually includes a place/date, greeting, a clear message in paragraphs, a closing and the writer's name. The exact format may vary by task.

cards.title: Information and viewpoint
cards.content: The text presents knowledge through a grandmother's friendly voice. Distinguish what the letter says about traditional use from what is scientifically established.

cards.title: Reading vocabulary
facts: An aromatic plant part or substance used to flavour food.
A treatment or measure intended to relieve a problem.
A practice or knowledge passed through generations.

cards.title: Critical thinking
cards.question: Why should traditional spice uses be distinguished from medical advice?
cards.answer: Because a traditional practice is not automatically proven to treat an illness; serious health concerns need guidance from a qualified professional.

cards.title: Story / poem idea
cards.content: Prabhat is obsessed with winning and even cheats during a game. Surya's cheerful attitude after losing helps Prabhat realise that enjoying the game and playing fairly matter more than winning.

cards.title: Notice and explain
cards.content: Compare Prabhat's attitude before and after meeting Surya. Look for the moment that changes his understanding of sportsmanship.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What causes Prabhat's change of heart?
cards.answer: Surya enjoys playing even after losing, which makes Prabhat realise that fair play, effort and enjoyment matter more than the result.

cards.title: Character contrast
facts: Focuses strongly on winning and cheats during a game.
Enjoys playing and remains cheerful even after losing.
Surya's attitude makes Prabhat reconsider what sport should mean.
Prabhat learns to value fair play and enjoyment.

cards.title: Theme: sportsmanship
cards.content: Sportsmanship means playing fairly, respecting opponents and officials, accepting results and valuing effort and teamwork alongside winning.

left.heading: Winning at any cost
left.content: May encourage cheating, pressure and disrespect; it weakens the purpose of sport.

right.heading: Good sportsmanship
right.content: Values fair play, effort, learning, teamwork and respect whether one wins or loses.

cards.title: Character development
cards.content: Prabhat's change is shown through a shift in attitude. A good answer should explain what he believed at first, what he observed and what he understood afterwards.

cards.title: Theme check
cards.question: What does Surya teach Prabhat without giving him a lecture?
cards.answer: Surya's cheerful acceptance of losing shows that enjoyment, fair play and effort matter more than winning alone.

cards.title: Story / poem idea
cards.content: The poem describes children playing until the day ends. Personification gives the natural end of the game a playful sense of victory.

cards.title: Notice and explain
cards.content: Notice the poem's images of play, evening and tiredness. Explain how personification makes the ending memorable.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: Who is described as the winner at the end of the poem, and why?
cards.answer: Night is playfully presented as the winner because darkness ends the children's game.

cards.title: Central image of the poem
cards.content: Children play energetically with the passing day. Evening and night bring the game to an end; the poem playfully presents the natural cycle as part of the contest.

cards.title: Personification and imagery
facts: Night or natural elements are described as if they can act like people.
Words create pictures of children playing and the changing sky.
Playful and lively, with a gentle sense of the day ending.

cards.title: Theme: play and time
cards.content: The poem captures the joy of play and the way time passes. Even a happy activity must pause when daylight fades.

left.heading: Literal
left.content: Night arrives as the sky becomes dark and children stop playing.

right.heading: Figurative
right.content: Night is imagined as a competitor that wins by ending the game.

cards.title: Poetic device
cards.question: How does personification make the ending memorable?
cards.answer: It makes night seem like a playful opponent that can win the game, turning the arrival of darkness into an imaginative event.

cards.title: Story / poem idea
cards.content: The text presents yoga as a practice that connects body and mind. It describes yoga's Indian roots and its role in physical fitness, calmness and well-being.

cards.title: Notice and explain
cards.content: Remember that yoga includes more than physical postures; breathing, attention and balanced habits are also important.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What does the word yoga suggest in the text?
cards.answer: It comes from a Sanskrit root meaning to join or unite, expressing harmony between body and mind and between thought and action.

cards.title: Yoga: key components
facts: Ethical and personal disciplines in classical yoga traditions.
Yoga can support balance, flexibility, attention and calm when practised safely.

cards.title: Yoga is more than exercise
cards.content: The text presents yoga as a way of harmonising body and mind. Physical postures are one part; breathing, attention, discipline and balanced living also matter.

cards.title: Safe practice
facts: Learn unfamiliar postures from a qualified teacher.
Do not force a stretch or ignore pain.
Gentle, regular practice is better than unsafe overexertion.
Adapt practice to age, ability and health.

cards.title: Origin and meaning
cards.content: The word yoga comes from a Sanskrit root often explained as 'to join' or 'to unite'. The text connects the practice with India's cultural and knowledge traditions.

cards.title: Meaning check
cards.question: What does the word yoga suggest in the text?
cards.answer: It suggests joining or uniting, expressing harmony between body and mind and balanced living.

cards.title: Story / poem idea
cards.content: The text celebrates India's varied landscapes, languages, arts, food and traditions, showing how many local cultures contribute to a shared national identity.

cards.title: Notice and explain
cards.content: Use examples from the text to explain diversity. Avoid treating one custom, language or region as representative of the whole country.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: How can India's diversity be seen in everyday life?
cards.answer: Through its many languages, foods, clothing styles, art forms, festivals, landscapes and regional traditions.

cards.title: Ways India is diverse
facts: Mountains, deserts, plains, forests, coasts and islands.
Music, dance, crafts, painting and architecture.

cards.title: The main message
cards.content: The text celebrates India's many cultures and landscapes. It encourages readers to appreciate regional differences while recognising shared belonging.

cards.title: Use examples, not stereotypes
cards.content: When describing a region, use examples from the text and avoid claiming that every person from that region follows the same food, language or custom.

cards.title: Descriptive writing techniques
facts: Name places, foods, art forms and landscapes.
Use details about colour, sound, taste and movement.
Show how places or practices are alike or different.

cards.title: Comprehension check
cards.question: Give two examples of India's cultural diversity mentioned in the text's theme.
cards.answer: Examples include languages, regional foods, clothing, festivals, music, dance and art forms.

cards.title: Story / poem idea
cards.content: The poem uses the movement and colours of kites to create a lively picture of the sky and the joy of flying them.

cards.title: Notice and explain
cards.content: Look for visual imagery, movement words and sound patterns. Explain how the images help the reader picture the scene.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: Which poetic device helps readers picture colourful kites moving in the sky?
cards.answer: Imagery: descriptive words create a clear picture of the kites, their colours and their movement.

cards.title: Poetic imagery
facts: Colour, shape and movement of kites in the sky.
The kite rises, dips, sways or dances with the wind.
A sense of freedom, joy and play.
Words and rhythm can imitate the lively outdoor scene.

cards.title: Central idea
cards.content: The poem uses kites and the sky to capture the excitement of flying kites. The movement of the kite reflects the energy and imagination of children.

cards.title: Personification and comparison
cards.content: A poet may describe a kite as if it dances or plays. Such language helps readers imagine movement and gives the scene life.

cards.title: Vocabulary to notice
facts: Move lightly and quickly in the air.
A sudden strong movement of wind.

cards.title: Poetry check
cards.question: Which poetic feature helps readers picture colourful kites moving in the sky?
cards.answer: Imagery: descriptive words create a clear picture of the kites and their movement.

chapters.title: Ila Sachani: Embroidering Dreams with her Feet
chapters.subtitle: Poorvi · Culture and Tradition

cards.title: Story / poem idea
cards.content: Ila Sachani, from Gujarat, develops great skill in Kathiawar embroidery by learning to use her feet because she cannot use her hands in the usual way. Her family encourages her talent.

cards.title: Notice and explain
cards.content: Focus on the support she receives, the skill she develops and how determination opens opportunities. Do not reduce her story to disability alone; recognise her artistry.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: How did Ila Sachani learn to create embroidery despite the challenge she faced?
cards.answer: With encouragement from her mother and grandmother, she practised and developed the skill of using her feet to create intricate embroidery.

cards.title: Ila Sachani: key details
facts: She could not use her hands in the usual way.
She learned to create intricate embroidery using her feet.
Encouragement and practice helped her develop her talent.

cards.title: Theme: determination and skill
cards.content: The account focuses on Ila's creativity, training, persistence and artistry. Her achievement should be understood as skilled work, not reduced only to the challenge she faced.

cards.title: Role of family support
cards.content: Her mother and grandmother help her learn and practise. Encouragement, access and patient training can help a person develop talent.

cards.title: Inference
cards.question: How did Ila Sachani develop her embroidery skill?
cards.answer: With encouragement from her family, she practised and developed the ability to create detailed embroidery using her feet.

cards.title: Story / poem idea
cards.content: The text honours soldiers who gave their lives in service of the country and reminds readers why remembrance, gratitude and peace matter.

cards.title: Notice and explain
cards.content: Identify the memorial's purpose and the values it represents. Connect remembrance with respect for those who serve.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: Why is a National War Memorial important?
cards.answer: It honours and remembers soldiers' service and sacrifice, helping citizens express gratitude and reflect on peace and responsibility.

cards.title: Purpose of the National War Memorial
facts: Honours soldiers who lost their lives in service.
Provides a place for citizens to remember their contribution.
Connects visitors with the country's military history.
Encourages reflection on courage, duty and peace.

cards.title: Respectful language
cards.content: When writing about soldiers and sacrifice, use accurate, respectful language. Explain the memorial's purpose rather than relying only on emotional adjectives.

cards.title: A visit or description can include
facts: Describe where the memorial is and what visitors see.
Explain how names or inscriptions preserve memory.
State what the memorial makes a visitor think about.

cards.title: Theme: memory and responsibility
cards.content: A memorial is not only a structure; it preserves collective memory and invites people to think about service, responsibility and the value of peace.

cards.title: Purpose check
cards.question: Why is a National War Memorial important?
cards.answer: It honours and remembers soldiers' service and sacrifice and encourages citizens to reflect on gratitude, responsibility and peace.

cards.title: मुख्य भाव
cards.content: कविता में मातृभूमि के प्रति प्रेम, सम्मान और कृतज्ञता का भाव व्यक्त होता है। देश की प्रकृति, संस्कृति और लोगों से जुड़ाव कविता का मुख्य आधार है।

cards.title: ध्यान दें
cards.content: कविता पढ़ते समय देश के प्रति भाव, चित्रात्मक शब्दों और कवि के संदेश को पहचानें। अपने शब्दों में बताएं कि मातृभूमि हमारे लिए क्यों महत्त्वपूर्ण है।

cards.title: त्वरित पुनरावृत्ति
cards.question: ‘मातृभूमि’ कविता का मुख्य भाव क्या है?
cards.answer: मातृभूमि के प्रति प्रेम, सम्मान और उसके प्रति अपने कर्तव्यों का बोध।

cards.title: कविता के मुख्य बिंदु
facts: मातृभूमि के प्रति प्रेम, सम्मान और कृतज्ञता।
देश की धरती, नदियाँ, पर्वत और प्राकृतिक सौंदर्य का महत्त्व।
देश की संस्कृति और लोगों से जुड़ाव।
मातृभूमि के प्रति जिम्मेदारी और सेवा का भाव।

cards.title: भाव और संदेश
cards.content: कविता केवल देश की प्रशंसा नहीं करती; यह अपने देश के प्रति प्रेम के साथ उसके प्रति जिम्मेदारी निभाने की प्रेरणा भी देती है।

cards.title: कविता की भाषा
cards.content: प्रकृति और मातृभूमि से जुड़े चित्रात्मक शब्द कविता में भाव जगाते हैं। उत्तर लिखते समय कविता के शब्दों या भावों का सहारा लेकर अर्थ स्पष्ट करें।

cards.title: भावार्थ प्रश्न
cards.question: ‘मातृभूमि’ कविता में मातृभूमि के प्रति कौन-से भाव व्यक्त होते हैं?
cards.answer: प्रेम, सम्मान, कृतज्ञता और मातृभूमि के प्रति अपने कर्तव्यों का बोध।

cards.title: अपने शब्दों में
cards.question: मातृभूमि के प्रति प्रेम केवल भावना क्यों नहीं, जिम्मेदारी भी है?
cards.answer: क्योंकि देश के प्रति प्रेम का अर्थ उसके लोगों, प्रकृति, संस्कृति और सार्वजनिक संसाधनों का सम्मान करना तथा अपने कर्तव्यों का पालन करना भी है।

cards.title: मुख्य भाव
cards.content: ‘गोल’ संस्मरण में हॉकी के अनुभवों के माध्यम से खेल के प्रति लगन, अभ्यास, अनुशासन और टीम भावना का महत्त्व उभरता है।

cards.title: ध्यान दें
cards.content: घटना-क्रम याद रखें और समझें कि सफलता केवल व्यक्तिगत कौशल से नहीं, बल्कि अभ्यास और साथियों के सहयोग से भी मिलती है।

cards.title: त्वरित पुनरावृत्ति
cards.question: खेल में टीम भावना क्यों आवश्यक है?
cards.answer: टीम भावना से खिलाड़ी एक-दूसरे का सहयोग करते हैं, मिलकर रणनीति बनाते हैं और सामूहिक लक्ष्य प्राप्त करते हैं।

cards.title: पाठ के मुख्य बिंदु
facts: हॉकी के खेल और खिलाड़ी के अनुभव।
अभ्यास, अनुशासन, लगन और टीम भावना।
व्यक्तिगत कौशल के साथ-साथ साथियों का सहयोग जरूरी।
लगातार अभ्यास से कौशल और आत्मविश्वास बढ़ता है।

cards.title: टीम भावना
cards.content: टीम खेल में खिलाड़ी एक-दूसरे पर भरोसा करते हैं, पास देते हैं, रणनीति अपनाते हैं और सामूहिक लक्ष्य के लिए काम करते हैं।

cards.title: संस्मरण की विशेषता
cards.content: संस्मरण में लेखक अपने अनुभवों और यादों को वर्णित करता है। इसमें घटनाओं के साथ लेखक की अनुभूति और दृष्टिकोण भी महत्त्वपूर्ण होते हैं।

left.heading: व्यक्तिगत कौशल
left.content: खिलाड़ी की अपनी तकनीक, गति, अभ्यास और निर्णय क्षमता।

right.heading: टीमवर्क
right.content: साथियों के साथ तालमेल, सहयोग, संवाद और साझा रणनीति।

cards.title: पाठ से सीख
cards.question: खेल में टीम भावना क्यों आवश्यक है?
cards.answer: टीम भावना से खिलाड़ी एक-दूसरे का सहयोग करते हैं, मिलकर रणनीति बनाते हैं और सामूहिक लक्ष्य प्राप्त करते हैं।

cards.title: मुख्य भाव
cards.content: कविता में वर्षा की पहली बूँद से प्रकृति में आने वाली ताजगी और जीवन की नई उमंग का चित्रण है।

cards.title: ध्यान दें
cards.content: कविता के प्रकृति-चित्रों और ध्वनि/दृश्य बिंबों पर ध्यान दें। बताएं कि पहली वर्षा धरती और मन को कैसे प्रभावित करती है।

cards.title: त्वरित पुनरावृत्ति
cards.question: पहली बूँद के आने से प्रकृति में क्या परिवर्तन दिखाई देता है?
cards.answer: धरती में ताजगी आती है, मिट्टी की सुगंध फैलती है और पेड़-पौधे तथा जीव-जगत प्रसन्न और सक्रिय हो उठते हैं।

cards.title: कविता के बिंब
facts: वर्षा के आरंभ और नई ताजगी का संकेत।
वर्षा से मिट्टी में सुगंध और जीवन का संचार।
पेड़-पौधों और जीव-जगत में नई उमंग।

cards.title: चित्रात्मक भाषा
cards.content: कवि दृश्य, गंध और ध्वनि से जुड़े शब्दों द्वारा पहली वर्षा का अनुभव जीवंत बनाता है। ऐसे शब्दों को पहचानकर बताएं कि वे कौन-सा दृश्य या अनुभूति जगाते हैं।

cards.title: कविता का केंद्रीय भाव
cards.content: पहली वर्षा केवल मौसम का बदलाव नहीं, बल्कि प्रकृति में ताजगी और मन में प्रसन्नता लाने वाला अनुभव है।

cards.title: कविता पढ़ते समय ध्यान दें
facts: कौन-से शब्द आँखों के सामने दृश्य बनाते हैं?
कविता आनंद, आश्चर्य या शांति में से कौन-सा भाव जगाती है?
प्रकृति का वर्णन करने वाले विशेषण और क्रियाएँ।

cards.title: केंद्रीय भाव
cards.question: पहली बूँद के आने से प्रकृति में क्या परिवर्तन दिखाई देता है?
cards.answer: धरती में ताजगी आती है, मिट्टी की सुगंध फैलती है और पेड़-पौधे तथा जीव-जगत प्रसन्न और सक्रिय हो उठते हैं।

cards.title: मुख्य भाव
cards.content: कहानी में बाबा भारती का घोड़ा सुल्तान और खड़गसिंह की घटना के माध्यम से दया, विश्वास और मानवीयता का संदेश मिलता है। बाबा भारती घोड़े से अधिक मनुष्य के भीतर की अच्छाई को महत्त्व देते हैं।

cards.title: ध्यान दें
cards.content: बाबा भारती और खड़गसिंह के व्यवहार में आए परिवर्तन की तुलना करें। कहानी का शीर्षक बाहरी हार के बजाय नैतिक विजय की ओर संकेत करता है।

cards.title: त्वरित पुनरावृत्ति
cards.question: कहानी में ‘हार की जीत’ किस अर्थ में है?
cards.answer: बाबा भारती का विश्वास और करुणा अंततः खड़गसिंह के मन को बदल देते हैं। नैतिकता और मानवता की जीत होती है।

cards.title: मुख्य पात्र और घटनाएँ
facts: सुल्तान घोड़े से गहरा प्रेम करते हैं और दया-विश्वास को महत्त्व देते हैं।
घोड़ा पाने के लिए छल करता है।
बाबा भारती की करुणा और विश्वास खड़गसिंह के मन को प्रभावित करते हैं।

cards.title: कहानी का संदेश
cards.content: कहानी बताती है कि सच्ची मानवता, दया और विश्वास किसी के भीतर परिवर्तन ला सकते हैं। दूसरों की सहायता करते समय स्वार्थ से ऊपर उठना महत्त्वपूर्ण है।

cards.title: शीर्षक का अर्थ
cards.content: ‘हार’ बाहरी घटना या घोड़े के खोने से जुड़ी दिखती है, लेकिन अंततः बाबा भारती की करुणा और खड़गसिंह के बदलते मन से नैतिक विजय सामने आती है।

left.heading: खड़गसिंह का छल
left.content: अपना स्वार्थ पूरा करने के लिए असहाय व्यक्ति का रूप धारण करना।

right.heading: बाबा भारती की करुणा
right.content: दूसरे की पीड़ा देखकर सहायता करना और मानवता पर विश्वास बनाए रखना।

cards.title: चरित्र-चित्रण
cards.question: बाबा भारती के चरित्र की दो विशेषताएँ बताइए।
cards.answer: वे दयालु और करुणामय हैं; वे सुल्तान से प्रेम करते हैं और मानवता तथा विश्वास को महत्त्व देते हैं।

cards.title: मुख्य भाव
cards.content: रहीम के दोहों में विनम्रता, प्रेम, संबंधों की मर्यादा, परोपकार और व्यवहार-कुशलता जैसे जीवन-मूल्य सरल उदाहरणों से समझाए गए हैं।

cards.title: ध्यान दें
cards.content: हर दोहे का सरल अर्थ लिखें और उससे मिलने वाली सीख को अपने जीवन के उदाहरण से जोड़ें।

cards.title: त्वरित पुनरावृत्ति
cards.question: रहीम के दोहे हमें किस प्रकार का व्यवहार अपनाने की सीख देते हैं?
cards.answer: विनम्र, संवेदनशील और परोपकारी व्यवहार; संबंधों का सम्मान और दूसरों की भावनाओं का ध्यान।

cards.title: रहीम के दोहों में जीवन-मूल्य
facts: अहंकार से बचना और दूसरों का सम्मान करना।
संबंधों को सावधानी और संवेदना से निभाना।
बात और व्यवहार में संतुलन रखना।
समय, परिस्थिति और व्यक्ति के अनुसार उचित व्यवहार करना।

cards.title: दोहा छंद
cards.content: दोहा हिंदी काव्य का एक प्रसिद्ध छंद है। इसमें दो पंक्तियाँ होती हैं और प्रत्येक पंक्ति में निश्चित मात्रिक व्यवस्था होती है।

cards.title: नीति-काव्य
cards.content: रहीम के दोहे छोटे और सरल रूप में गहरी जीवन-सीख देते हैं। दोहे का अर्थ समझाते समय उसके शब्दार्थ और व्यावहारिक संदेश दोनों लिखें।

cards.title: दोहा का भावार्थ कैसे लिखें
steps: दोहा ध्यान से पढ़ें और कठिन शब्दों का अर्थ समझें।
कवि किस व्यवहार या जीवन-मूल्य की बात कर रहे हैं, पहचानें।
भाव को सरल भाषा में अपने शब्दों में लिखें।
एक छोटा उदाहरण देकर संदेश स्पष्ट करें।

cards.title: जीवन-मूल्य
cards.question: रहीम के दोहे हमें किस प्रकार का व्यवहार अपनाने की सीख देते हैं?
cards.answer: विनम्र, संवेदनशील और परोपकारी व्यवहार; संबंधों का सम्मान और दूसरों की भावनाओं का ध्यान।

cards.title: मुख्य भाव
cards.content: इस आत्मकथात्मक पाठ में माँ के स्नेह, त्याग, साहस और संस्कारों का प्रभाव सामने आता है। माँ का मार्गदर्शन व्यक्ति के चरित्र और जीवन-मूल्यों को आकार देता है।

cards.title: ध्यान दें
cards.content: लेखक की माँ के गुणों को पाठ के प्रसंगों से समझाएँ। केवल विशेषण लिखने के बजाय बताएं कि उनके व्यवहार से कौन-सा गुण प्रकट होता है।

cards.title: त्वरित पुनरावृत्ति
cards.question: लेखक के जीवन पर माँ का क्या प्रभाव पड़ा?
cards.answer: माँ के स्नेह, साहस और संस्कारों ने लेखक को प्रेरित किया तथा उसके व्यक्तित्व और जीवन-मूल्यों को मजबूत बनाया।

cards.title: माँ के व्यक्तित्व के गुण
facts: परिवार के प्रति प्रेम और देखभाल।
दूसरों की भलाई के लिए अपना आराम छोड़ना।
बच्चों को अच्छे व्यवहार और जीवन-मूल्य सिखाना।

cards.title: आत्मकथात्मक लेखन
cards.content: आत्मकथात्मक पाठ में लेखक अपने जीवन, परिवार या अनुभवों से जुड़ी घटनाएँ बताता है। निजी स्मृतियों के साथ भावनाएँ और सीख भी महत्त्वपूर्ण होती हैं।

cards.title: माँ का प्रभाव
cards.content: माँ का व्यवहार, सलाह और उदाहरण बच्चे के व्यक्तित्व को आकार देते हैं। पाठ में बताए गए प्रसंगों के आधार पर उनके गुणों को समझना चाहिए।

cards.title: चरित्र-चित्रण लिखें
steps: पात्र के दो या तीन प्रमुख गुण चुनें।
हर गुण के समर्थन में पाठ का एक प्रसंग बताएं।
बताएं कि उस व्यवहार से कौन-सा गुण प्रकट होता है।
अंत में पात्र का समग्र प्रभाव लिखें।

cards.title: पाठ-बोध
cards.question: लेखक के जीवन पर माँ का क्या प्रभाव पड़ा?
cards.answer: माँ के स्नेह, साहस और संस्कारों ने लेखक को प्रेरित किया तथा उसके व्यक्तित्व और जीवन-मूल्यों को मजबूत बनाया।

cards.title: मुख्य भाव
cards.content: कविता में दीप जलाने का प्रतीक आशा, ज्ञान, साहस और निरंतर अच्छे कार्य करते रहने का संदेश देता है।

cards.title: ध्यान दें
cards.content: दीपक को केवल वस्तु न मानें; कविता में उसका प्रतीकात्मक अर्थ समझें। बताएं कि कठिन समय में आशा बनाए रखना क्यों जरूरी है।

cards.title: त्वरित पुनरावृत्ति
cards.question: कविता में दीप जलाने का प्रतीकात्मक अर्थ क्या है?
cards.answer: अंधकार और निराशा को दूर करके आशा, ज्ञान और सकारात्मकता फैलाते रहना।

cards.title: दीपक के प्रतीकात्मक अर्थ
facts: दूसरों के जीवन में भलाई और प्रेरणा फैलाना।

cards.title: प्रतीक का प्रयोग
cards.content: कविता में दीपक केवल जलने वाली वस्तु नहीं है। वह आशा, ज्ञान और निरंतर अच्छे कार्य करते रहने का प्रतीक बनता है।

cards.title: कविता का स्वर
cards.content: कविता प्रेरणात्मक है। इसमें पाठक को निराश न होकर लगातार प्रयास करते रहने और दूसरों के जीवन में प्रकाश फैलाने का संदेश मिलता है।

cards.title: कविता से जुड़े शब्द
facts: अज्ञान, निराशा या कठिनाई का प्रतीक हो सकता है।
ज्ञान, आशा और सकारात्मकता का प्रतीक।
निरंतर प्रयास या त्याग का संकेत।

cards.title: प्रतीकात्मक अर्थ
cards.question: कविता में दीप जलाने का प्रतीकात्मक अर्थ क्या है?
cards.answer: अंधकार और निराशा को दूर करके आशा, ज्ञान और सकारात्मकता फैलाते रहना।

cards.title: मुख्य भाव
cards.content: पाठ में असम की दो विशिष्ट नृत्य परंपराओं—सत्रिया और बिहू—का परिचय मिलता है। ये राज्य की सांस्कृतिक पहचान, इतिहास और सामुदायिक जीवन से जुड़ी हैं।

cards.title: ध्यान दें
cards.content: सत्रिया और बिहू की उत्पत्ति, अवसर, वेशभूषा और प्रस्तुति के अंतर को अलग-अलग बिंदुओं में लिखें।

cards.title: त्वरित पुनरावृत्ति
cards.question: सत्रिया और बिहू नृत्य में एक प्रमुख अंतर बताइए।
cards.answer: सत्रिया असम की शास्त्रीय नृत्य परंपरा है, जबकि बिहू असम के लोकजीवन और बिहू उत्सवों से जुड़ा लोकनृत्य है।

cards.title: सत्रिया और बिहू
facts: असम की शास्त्रीय नृत्य परंपरा; सत्रों और वैष्णव सांस्कृतिक परंपरा से जुड़ी।
असम के लोकजीवन और बिहू उत्सवों से जुड़ा लोकनृत्य।
दोनों असम की पहचान और सांस्कृतिक विरासत को दर्शाते हैं।

left.heading: सत्रिया
left.content: शास्त्रीय नृत्य परंपरा, जिसकी विशिष्ट शैली, संगीत और अनुशासित प्रस्तुति है।

right.heading: बिहू
right.content: लोकनृत्य, जो उत्सव, सामुदायिक आनंद और कृषि-जीवन से जुड़ा है।

cards.title: लोक और शास्त्रीय परंपरा
cards.content: लोक परंपराएँ समुदाय के जीवन और उत्सवों से विकसित होती हैं। शास्त्रीय परंपराओं में विशिष्ट नियम, प्रशिक्षण और शैलीगत संरचना होती है।

cards.title: संस्कृति और पहचान
cards.content: नृत्य, संगीत, वेशभूषा और त्योहार किसी क्षेत्र की सांस्कृतिक पहचान को व्यक्त करते हैं।

cards.title: तुलना प्रश्न
cards.question: सत्रिया और बिहू नृत्य में एक प्रमुख अंतर बताइए।
cards.answer: सत्रिया असम की शास्त्रीय नृत्य परंपरा है, जबकि बिहू असम के लोकजीवन और बिहू उत्सवों से जुड़ा लोकनृत्य है।

cards.title: मुख्य भाव
cards.content: सूरदास के पद में बालकृष्ण की चंचलता और माँ यशोदा के साथ उनका नटखट संवाद दिखाई देता है। कृष्ण माखन खाने से इनकार करते हुए भोलेपन से अपनी बात रखते हैं।

cards.title: ध्यान दें
cards.content: कृष्ण की बाल-लीलाओं, संवाद की चंचलता और वात्सल्य रस को पहचानें। पद की भाषा में लोक-जीवन की सहजता भी दिखाई देती है।

cards.title: त्वरित पुनरावृत्ति
cards.question: कृष्ण यशोदा से क्या कहते हैं?
cards.answer: कृष्ण कहते हैं कि उन्होंने माखन नहीं खाया और अपनी मासूमियत भरे तर्कों से माँ को समझाने का प्रयास करते हैं।

cards.title: कृष्ण और यशोदा
facts: माखन खाने से इनकार करते हुए भोलेपन से अपनी बात रखते हैं।
कृष्ण से प्रश्न करती हैं और उनके व्यवहार को समझने का प्रयास करती हैं।

cards.title: वात्सल्य रस
cards.content: माता-पिता या बड़े व्यक्ति का बच्चे के प्रति स्नेह वात्सल्य भाव कहलाता है। बालकृष्ण और यशोदा का संवाद इस भाव को सहज रूप से व्यक्त करता है।

cards.title: संवाद की चंचलता
cards.content: कृष्ण के तर्क और भोलेपन से भरे उत्तर पद को रोचक बनाते हैं। संवाद से बाल-स्वभाव और माँ-बेटे का स्नेह उभरता है।

cards.title: भाव-बोध
cards.question: कृष्ण यशोदा से क्या कहते हैं?
cards.answer: कृष्ण कहते हैं कि उन्होंने माखन नहीं खाया और अपनी मासूमियत भरे तर्कों से माँ को समझाने का प्रयास करते हैं।

cards.title: मुख्य भाव
cards.content: देवगढ़ रियासत के लिए नया दीवान चुनना है। सरदार सुजानसिंह उम्मीदवारों की केवल डिग्री नहीं, बल्कि उनके आचरण, दया, साहस और कर्तव्यनिष्ठा को परखते हैं। पंडित जानकीनाथ घायल होने पर भी एक गरीब किसान की गाड़ी दलदल से निकालने में मदद करते हैं और इसी मानवीय व्यवहार के कारण चुने जाते हैं।

cards.title: ध्यान दें
cards.content: कहानी में उम्मीदवारों के दिखावटी शिष्टाचार और जानकीनाथ के वास्तविक सेवाभाव का अंतर समझें। दीवान चुनने की कसौटी—दया, उदारता, आत्मबल और कर्तव्यनिष्ठा—घटनाओं से स्पष्ट करें।

cards.title: त्वरित पुनरावृत्ति
cards.question: पंडित जानकीनाथ को देवगढ़ का दीवान क्यों चुना गया?
cards.answer: उन्होंने स्वयं घायल होने के बावजूद एक गरीब किसान की अनाज से भरी गाड़ी को दलदल से निकालने में मदद की। उनके व्यवहार से दया, साहस, उदारता और कर्तव्यनिष्ठा प्रकट हुई।

cards.title: मुख्य पात्र और चयन
facts: देवगढ़ के लिए योग्य दीवान चुनने की जिम्मेदारी निभाते हैं।
अपनी योग्यता और व्यवहार से चयनित होना चाहते हैं।
घायल होने पर भी गरीब किसान की गाड़ी निकालने में सहायता करते हैं।

cards.title: कहानी का केंद्रीय विचार
cards.content: किसी व्यक्ति की वास्तविक योग्यता केवल डिग्री या दिखावे से नहीं, बल्कि कठिन परिस्थिति में उसके व्यवहार और मानवीय गुणों से पहचानी जाती है।

left.heading: दिखावा
left.content: लोगों के सामने अच्छा दिखाई देने की कोशिश, जो वास्तविक व्यवहार से मेल न भी खाए।

right.heading: वास्तविक चरित्र
right.content: बिना लाभ की अपेक्षा के कठिन समय में किया गया सही और संवेदनशील कार्य।

cards.title: घटना-क्रम याद रखें
steps: देवगढ़ के लिए नए दीवान का चयन होना है।
उम्मीदवारों का व्यवहार और गुण परखे जाते हैं।
एक किसान की गाड़ी दलदल में फँस जाती है।
जानकीनाथ स्वयं घायल होने के बावजूद सहायता करते हैं।
उनके व्यवहार से उनके मानवीय गुण प्रकट होते हैं और उनका चयन होता है।

cards.title: चरित्र-आधारित प्रश्न
cards.question: पंडित जानकीनाथ को देवगढ़ का दीवान क्यों चुना गया?
cards.answer: उन्होंने स्वयं घायल होने के बावजूद एक गरीब किसान की अनाज से भरी गाड़ी को दलदल से निकालने में मदद की। उनके व्यवहार से दया, साहस, उदारता और कर्तव्यनिष्ठा प्रकट हुई।

cards.title: मुख्य भाव
cards.content: कविता में महाराणा प्रताप के घोड़े चेतक की निष्ठा, साहस और स्वामीभक्ति का वर्णन है। संकट की घड़ी में चेतक का धैर्य और बलिदान वीरता का उदाहरण बनता है।

cards.title: ध्यान दें
cards.content: कविता में चेतक के गुणों को घटनाओं से जोड़ें। वीरता के साथ निष्ठा और त्याग के भाव को भी समझें।

cards.title: त्वरित पुनरावृत्ति
cards.question: चेतक को वीर और निष्ठावान क्यों कहा गया है?
cards.answer: उसने संकट में महाराणा प्रताप का साथ नहीं छोड़ा और अपनी शक्ति तथा साहस से उन्हें सुरक्षित पहुँचाने में योगदान दिया।

cards.title: चेतक के गुण
facts: कठिन परिस्थिति में तेज और कुशल गति।
स्वामी की रक्षा के लिए स्वयं कष्ट सहना।

cards.title: वीर रस
cards.content: वीर रस में साहस, उत्साह, पराक्रम और कर्तव्य के लिए संघर्ष का भाव प्रमुख होता है। चेतक की वीरता का वर्णन इसी भाव को जगाता है।

cards.title: पशु के प्रति संवेदना
cards.content: कविता चेतक को केवल घोड़ा नहीं, बल्कि निष्ठावान साथी के रूप में प्रस्तुत करती है। इससे मनुष्य और पशु के संबंध में विश्वास और संवेदना का महत्त्व दिखता है।

cards.title: कविता का संदेश
facts: दूसरे की रक्षा के लिए अपना हित पीछे रखना।

cards.title: काव्य-बोध
cards.question: चेतक को वीर और निष्ठावान क्यों कहा गया है?
cards.answer: उसने संकट में महाराणा प्रताप का साथ नहीं छोड़ा और अपनी शक्ति तथा साहस से उन्हें सुरक्षित पहुँचाने में योगदान दिया।

cards.title: मुख्य भाव
cards.content: यात्रा-वृत्तांत में हिंद महासागर के एक द्वीप-समाज में भारतीय मूल के लोगों, भाषा, संस्कृति और परंपराओं की झलक मिलती है। प्रवास के बाद भी सांस्कृतिक संबंध कैसे बने रहते हैं, यह पाठ दिखाता है।

cards.title: ध्यान दें
cards.content: यात्रा-वृत्तांत में स्थान, लोगों, रीति-रिवाजों और लेखक के अनुभवों को पहचानें। भारत से दूर रहते हुए भी संस्कृति के बने रहने के उदाहरण खोजें।

cards.title: त्वरित पुनरावृत्ति
cards.question: ‘छोटा-सा हिंदुस्तान’ किस अर्थ में कहा गया है?
cards.answer: विदेश में बसे भारतीय मूल के लोगों ने अपनी भाषा, परंपराओं, त्योहारों और सांस्कृतिक पहचान को सँजोकर रखा है; इसलिए वहाँ भारत की झलक दिखाई देती है।

cards.title: यात्रा-वृत्तांत के मुख्य पहलू
facts: हिंद महासागर का द्वीप-समाज जहाँ भारतीय मूल के लोग बसे हैं।
दूर देश में भी सांस्कृतिक पहचान सँजोई जा सकती है।

cards.title: प्रवासी संस्कृति
cards.content: जब लोग अपने मूल स्थान से दूर बसते हैं, तब भी वे भाषा, त्योहार, भोजन, संगीत और पारिवारिक परंपराओं के माध्यम से अपनी सांस्कृतिक स्मृतियों को जीवित रख सकते हैं।

cards.title: यात्रा-वृत्तांत की विशेषता
cards.content: यात्रा-वृत्तांत में लेखक किसी स्थान का वर्णन अपने अनुभवों, अवलोकनों और वहाँ मिले लोगों के माध्यम से करता है। स्थान-वर्णन के साथ व्यक्तिगत अनुभूति भी महत्त्वपूर्ण है।

left.heading: भौगोलिक दूरी
left.content: मूल देश से दूर रहने के कारण जीवन की परिस्थितियाँ और परिवेश बदल जाते हैं।

right.heading: सांस्कृतिक जुड़ाव
right.content: भाषा, त्योहार, भोजन और परंपराएँ लोगों को अपनी जड़ों से जोड़े रख सकती हैं।

cards.title: शीर्षक का अर्थ
cards.question: ‘छोटा-सा हिंदुस्तान’ किस अर्थ में कहा गया है?
cards.answer: विदेश में बसे भारतीय मूल के लोगों ने अपनी भाषा, परंपराओं, त्योहारों और सांस्कृतिक पहचान को सँजोकर रखा है; इसलिए वहाँ भारत की झलक दिखाई देती है।

cards.title: मुख्य भाव
cards.content: पाठ पेड़ों के जीवन, प्रकृति में उनके योगदान और मनुष्य के साथ उनके संबंध पर ध्यान दिलाता है। पेड़ पर्यावरण, भोजन, छाया, हवा और अनेक जीवों के आश्रय के लिए महत्त्वपूर्ण हैं।

cards.title: ध्यान दें
cards.content: पेड़ों के लाभों को पर्यावरण, जीव-जगत और मानव जीवन के संदर्भ में अलग-अलग समझें। संरक्षण के व्यावहारिक उपाय भी सोचें।

cards.title: त्वरित पुनरावृत्ति
cards.question: पेड़ प्रकृति और मनुष्य के लिए क्यों आवश्यक हैं?
cards.answer: पेड़ हवा को शुद्ध करने, छाया और भोजन देने, मिट्टी बचाने, जलचक्र में मदद करने और अनेक जीवों को आश्रय देने में महत्त्वपूर्ण हैं।

cards.title: पेड़ों के प्रमुख लाभ
facts: कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड लेते हैं और प्रकाश-संश्लेषण में ऑक्सीजन छोड़ते हैं।
जड़ों से मिट्टी को बाँधने और कटाव कम करने में मदद।
वाष्पोत्सर्जन और स्थानीय जलचक्र में योगदान।
पक्षियों, कीटों और अन्य जीवों को भोजन व आश्रय।
फल, लकड़ी, छाया और अनेक उपयोगी संसाधन।

cards.title: प्रकृति से परस्पर संबंध
cards.content: पेड़, मिट्टी, जल, वायु, पशु-पक्षी और मनुष्य एक-दूसरे से जुड़े हैं। पेड़ों को नुकसान पहुँचने से कई प्राकृतिक प्रक्रियाएँ प्रभावित होती हैं।

cards.title: संरक्षण क्यों जरूरी है?
cards.content: पेड़ों की रक्षा केवल लकड़ी या फल बचाने के लिए नहीं, बल्कि जैव-विविधता, मिट्टी, जल और जलवायु के संतुलन के लिए भी आवश्यक है।

cards.title: पेड़ों की रक्षा के उपाय
facts: पौधों को उचित पानी और सुरक्षा देना।
कागज और लकड़ी का सोच-समझकर उपयोग।
पेड़ों और उनके आसपास के जीवों के आवास को बचाना।

cards.title: पर्यावरण प्रश्न
cards.question: पेड़ प्रकृति और मनुष्य के लिए क्यों आवश्यक हैं?
cards.answer: पेड़ हवा को शुद्ध करने, छाया और भोजन देने, मिट्टी बचाने, जलचक्र में मदद करने और अनेक जीवों को आश्रय देने में महत्त्वपूर्ण हैं।
